memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Tell the people that men and women alike are to ask their neighbors for
articles of silver and gold." - Ex 11:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is an unusual instruction. God tells the Israelites to ask their Egyptian
neighbours for silver and gold before they leave. It might sound strange to us,
but remember what these people were. They were slaves who had worked without
wages for generations. This was not theft. It was long-overdue payment for
centuries of forced labour.

God had promised Abraham that his descendants would come out of their affliction
"with great possessions" (Gen 15:14). Four hundred years later, God remembers
that exact word and keeps it.

There is something quietly moving about this. God does not only rescue His
people; He cares that they are not sent away empty-handed. He notices the years
that were stolen from them. He notices the labour nobody paid for.

If you are carrying an old injustice that no one ever acknowledged, God has
noticed. He is not indifferent to what was taken from you. The final settling of
accounts belongs to Him, and He does it perfectly (Rom 12:19). Our part is to
leave it in His hands rather than trying to collect the debt ourselves.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an injustice you are still carrying quietly?
2. Can you trust God to be the one who settles it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You see what others have not seen and remember what others have forgotten.
Help me to leave my unpaid debts in Your hands and trust Your justice. Amen.
